title: "Career performance and Finals audiences"
output: html_document

## Preliminary visualizations and findings

```{r analysis-setup, include=FALSE}
if (!file.exists("data/processed/12_CleanData.RData")) {
  stop("Run 11_DataCleaning.Rmd first, following README.md.")
}
load("data/processed/12_CleanData.RData")
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
colors <- c("Michael Jordan" = "#B33B43", "Kobe Bryant" = "#7255A5",
            "LeBron James" = "#247F87")
```

### Career production

```{r performance-table}
knitr::kable(career[c("Player", "Games", "TotalPoints", "PPG", "RPG", "APG")],
             digits = 1, row.names = FALSE)
```

```{r performance-plot}
values <- t(as.matrix(career[c("PPG", "RPG", "APG")]))
barplot(values, beside = TRUE, names.arg = career$Player,
        col = c("#24446A", "#6A9FB5", "#D0A548"),
        ylab = "Per game", main = "Regular-season career production",
        ylim = c(0, 36), legend.text = c("Points", "Rebounds", "Assists"),
        args.legend = list(x = "topright", bty = "n"))
```

Jordan has the highest career scoring average (30.1 PPG), while LeBron has
the highest rebound (7.5 RPG) and assist (7.4 APG) averages in this snapshot.
Kobe averaged 25.0 PPG, 5.2 RPG and 4.7 APG. These statistics describe different
contributions and do not measure defense, shot difficulty or era-adjusted value.

### Finals audiences

```{r audience-table}
knitr::kable(summary_all, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
 caption = "Series audience summaries in millions; equal weight per series")
```

```{r audience-boxplot}
boxplot(ViewersMillions ~ Player, data = finals,
        col = colors[sort(unique(finals$Player))],
        ylab = "Average U.S. viewers per game (millions)", xlab = "",
        main = "Finals-series audiences by player")
stripchart(ViewersMillions ~ Player, data = finals, vertical = TRUE,
           method = "stack", add = TRUE, pch = 19, col = "#253444")
```

Mean series audiences are approximately 25.23 million for Jordan, 16.78 million
for Kobe, and 16.24 million for LeBron. These are conditional on Finals
appearances and reflect team matchups and television eras. They do not establish
how many viewers each player caused to watch.

```{r audience-time}
plot(finals$FinalsYear, finals$ViewersMillions,
     col = colors[finals$Player], pch = ifelse(finals$PandemicYear, 17, 19),
     xlab = "Finals year", ylab = "Average U.S. viewers per game (millions)",
     main = "Finals audiences across television eras")
legend("topright", legend = names(colors), col = colors, pch = 19, bty = "n")
text(finals$FinalsYear[finals$PandemicYear],
     finals$ViewersMillions[finals$PandemicYear], "2020", pos = 3)
```

Player and era are closely connected in these records. The scatterplot helps
show this limitation; audience differences cannot be assigned to player identity
alone. Keep the valid 2020 bubble observation and examine its influence.

### Sensitivity to 2020

```{r sensitivity}
knitr::kable(summary_without_2020, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
 caption = "Series audience summaries excluding 2020")
```

Excluding 2020 raises LeBron's equal-series mean to about 17.20 million,
compared with 16.24 million when all his appearances are included. His mean then
exceeds Kobe's 16.78 million in this dataset. Jordan's and Kobe's results are
unchanged. This shows why the scope must be stated alongside any ranking.

### Jersey popularity: selected reporting periods

```{r jersey-table}
knitr::kable(jerseys[c("Player", "ReportDateOrYear", "SalesRank")],
             row.names = FALSE,
 caption = "Selected published jersey rankings; lower rank means higher placement")
```

In the cited 2003 list, Kobe ranked first and Jordan fourth. In the NBA's April
2011 release, LeBron ranked first and Kobe second; in April 2012, Kobe ranked
third and LeBron fourth. These are selected historical snapshots with differing
periods and retail scopes. They are not career sales totals. Units sold and
revenue are unavailable, so the current data cannot support a three-player
career jersey-sales ranking. Additional matched-period data would be needed.
